decisions.decision: ~/enough/ as a single self-contained install root (code + defaults + weights + venv + infoworld)
inputs: user explicitly modeled it after ~/.claude and ~/.gemini
simpler than splitting between /usr/local and ~/.config
one directory to back up, one to delete to reset

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: requires sudo + more moving parts; distinction rarely helps for a local-only tool
user explicitly wanted no dot — makes the dir discoverable in Finder and Terminal tab-completion

decisions.weighting_logic: Self-contained wins on simplicity. Users can still separate weights manually via symlink if they want weights on a different disk.

decisions.decision: Dev clone at /Users/m3u/METMcloud/METMroot/enough stays; ~/enough/ is a separate user-realistic install created by bootstrap.sh doing a fresh `git clone`
inputs: user's instinct was right — two checkouts on the same machine is normal git
testing bootstrap.sh requires a blank-slate target; the install dir serves that role
dev changes commit from the dev clone and propagate to the install via git pull

alternatives_considered.option: Move the dev clone into ~/enough, develop in place
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: conflates 'codebase' and 'user install' mental models; makes the 'nuke and reinstall' test impossible

decisions.weighting_logic: Separation is free (disk), saves confusion (mental model), and enables clean reinstalls.

decisions.decision: Refuse to run `enough` inside ~/enough/ or any subdirectory of it
inputs: skeleton would create symlinks pointing into the same tree
user data + install data shouldn't intermix

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: the resulting state is genuinely broken; fail-fast is kinder

alternatives_considered.option: Detect and create project at a subdirectory like ~/enough/projects/
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: surprising magic; violates 'explicit beats implicit'

decisions.weighting_logic: Follow spec; fail fast with a clear error and a suggested next command.

decisions.decision: bootstrap.sh with narration-at-each-step as a teaching tool
inputs: user explicitly: 'i want non-technical people to get slightly comfortable with the command line... and learn to fear it a little less'
each step already has a clear purpose; printing that purpose costs nothing

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: misses the pedagogical goal
weeks of work (signing, notarization, wizard screens) for a paradigm that's still shifting

decisions.weighting_logic: Bash script = 90% of the UX of a real installer at 2% of the cost. Real installer is a v1.0 investment.

decisions.decision: PATH wrapper at ~/.local/bin/enough (3 lines, execs `uv run --project ~/enough enough`)
inputs: most modern user-local binary conventions use ~/.local/bin
avoids sudo and brew ownership complications
uv handles venv activation transparently

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: needs sudo; fights brew ownership
only works in shells that sourced it; invisible to non-shell spawners like `open`

decisions.weighting_logic: Wrapper script is the most portable, hermetic approach. bootstrap.sh warns if ~/.local/bin isn't on PATH and prints the one-liner to add it.

decisions.decision: Defaults live as committed .md files in <repo>/defaults/, not as Python string constants in skeleton.py
inputs: user wants to edit defaults directly (e.g. `nvim ~/enough/defaults/paradigms/default.md`)
Python strings are invisible to normal tooling (grep, editors, diff)
the defaults/ tree IS the shape of a `.rness/` — reading it is self-documenting

alternatives_considered.option: Keep as Python strings, generate files on first run
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: editing requires a code change + redeploy; breaks the 'plain text all the way down' ethos

decisions.weighting_logic: Plain text is the project's language. Python strings were convenient for v0.0.1 when defaults were tiny; they're now 300-line policy files.
decisions.downstream_impact: skeleton.py exports back-compat string constants (AGENT_MD, POLICY_REQUESTS_MD, etc.) by re-reading defaults/ at import time, so any test or tool that imported the constants still works.

decisions.decision: _install_defaults_root() resolves relative to the package (__file__.parents[1] / 'defaults'), not a hardcoded ~/enough/
inputs: enough can be run from a dev clone OR from ~/enough (via the PATH wrapper)
in either case, the 'defaults/' is the sibling of the 'enough/' Python package
relative resolution means no import of HOME or env parsing — just filesystem topology

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: breaks dev workflow (when running from /Users/m3u/METMcloud/METMroot/enough, ~/enough might not exist or might be stale)
punt on the fix; requires users to set env correctly

decisions.weighting_logic: Resolve by topology, not config. If you moved the install somewhere else, it still works.

decisions.decision: Per-file mode (symlink vs copy) declared in a table (_SKELETON_PLAN), not inferred
inputs: AGENT.md / MOTIVATION.md diverge fast — copy
paradigms / policies / models / skills / routines — global upgradable — symlink
knowledge/user-profile.md — per-project, starts empty — copy but inlined template (not in defaults/)

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: forces user to click 'customize' every single time before writing anything to AGENT.md — friction against the primary use case
loses the upgrade-everywhere property of symlinks for cross-cutting conventions like paradigms

decisions.weighting_logic: Different files have different semantics. Encoding this as a table keeps the intent explicit and easy to change per-file.

decisions.decision: infoworld/ lives at ~/enough/infoworld/ (per-user, not per-install) and is symlinked into each project
inputs: user explicitly: 'users/the rness agent should always be able to read from the global root enough folder, including the infoworld/ folder, and also be able to write files into infoworld/personal'
all projects sharing the same grounded-knowledge store is the whole point

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: wiki/ and personal/ are user data, not template content; would pollute the repo with gigabytes
defeats the shared-knowledge design

decisions.weighting_logic: Shared state is the goal; symlink is the lightest-weight mechanism.

decisions.decision: ensure_global_infoworld() auto-creates ~/enough/infoworld/ + subdirs on first skeleton run (not in bootstrap.sh exclusively)
inputs: user might run enough from a dev clone without running bootstrap.sh
skeleton creation is the right time to ensure everything needed exists

alternatives_considered.option: Require bootstrap.sh first; fail if infoworld root missing
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: brittle for dev workflows; idempotent self-heal is friendlier

decisions.weighting_logic: Self-heal is the cleaner invariant: 'infoworld exists wherever you create a project'.

decisions.decision: Read allowlist is itself a policy file (.rness/policies/read-allowlist.md), symlinked in and customizable via the same 'customize for this project' flow
inputs: user's suggestion: 'maybe it can just be a third document in policies, read_allowlist.md'
consistency: policy files govern agent behavior; this is agent behavior; therefore policy file

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: requires code change to broaden access
breaks the plain-text ethos and the 'symlink / customize' primitive

decisions.weighting_logic: Turtles all the way down: the allowlist is policy, policy is markdown, markdown is editable via the UI. Nothing special-cased.

decisions.decision: Allowlist parser greps markdown bullets under `## allowlisted prefixes` — not a structured data file
inputs: users read and write markdown naturally; JSON/YAML is a mode switch
the policy doubles as documentation for both the user and the agent

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: duplicates information between the human-readable policy text and the machine-readable config

decisions.weighting_logic: If the policy text already shows the list to the reader, parsing it avoids drift between what the user sees and what the tool enforces.
decisions.downstream_impact: Parser is permissive: matches `- \`~/some/path/\`` or `- /some/path` bullets, ignores prose. Fragile if someone writes 'paths are things like - ~/whatever' in the section body.

decisions.decision: read_file honors the allowlist for absolute paths; shell remains unrestricted
inputs: shell was always the 'deliberate nuclear option'
restricting shell would require parsing arbitrary shell commands — fragile and easy to bypass

alternatives_considered.option: Parse shell commands for file references and allowlist-check them
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: brittle; shell expansion, pipes, and variables make this nearly impossible

alternatives_considered.option: Restrict shell to project-dir cwd (already the case) AND block commands starting with allowlist-touching paths
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: partial safety theater

decisions.weighting_logic: Two tools with different semantics: read_file is structured and audited, shell is raw power. Users who care about tight sandboxing should disable shell access entirely.

decisions.decision: Symlink rendering in the UI: italic + muted text, 'symlink → <target>' note in preview, 'customize for this project' button in place of 'edit'
inputs: user: 'we can show symlinked/uneditable defaults in italics or something, shouldn't be too hard to distinguish UI wise'
italic is the canonical typography for 'reference elsewhere'
explicit action button (not a silent refusal of edit) teaches the paradigm

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: iconography adds visual weight; italic is information-dense at zero cost

alternatives_considered.option: Make edit work on symlinks by writing through
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: violates 'global defaults can't be edited from project'

decisions.weighting_logic: Affordances match semantics. Editable = edit button. Not-editable-but-customizable = customize button. Both discoverable.

decisions.decision: Path-safety check uses LOGICAL composition (path_str against resolved project_root), not .resolve() on the target
inputs: initial impl called target.resolve() which followed in-tree symlinks out of the project, then rejected them as 'path escapes project dir'
the threat model is user-provided path strings with absolute-path or ../ escapes, not symlinks placed legitimately inside the project by skeleton gen

alternatives_considered.option: Keep .resolve() + add allowlist of known-external symlink targets
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: turns path-safety into a dynamic rule that depends on skeleton state

alternatives_considered.option: Don't create external symlinks (use bind mounts or hardlinks)
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: non-portable, surprising filesystem behavior

decisions.weighting_logic: Threat model is path-string injection. Symlinks placed by the harness itself are trusted. Tool-level allowlist is the real 'can the agent read here?' gate; server path-safety should only reject user-supplied paths that try to escape via string manipulation.
